intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is caused by homozygous mutation in the KIRREL1 gene (607428) on chromosome 1q23.1.

checks.claim: Nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is caused by homozygous mutation in the KIRREL1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe two unrelated families with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with homozygous mutations in the KIRREL1 gene.
checks.explanation: Paper reports homozygous KIRREL1 mutations causing SRNS; NPHS23 is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 gene is located on chromosome 1q23.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing identifies a homozygous mutation of KIRREL1 (p.Arg440Cys) that is positioned within the maximum NPL peak on chromosome 1 (arrowhead).
checks.explanation: Paper places KIRREL1 on chromosome 1; the band 1q23.1 is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is an autosomal recessive kidney disorder that presents with proteinuria and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (Solanki et al., 2019). Renal biopsy may show focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) or other glomerular changes (Solanki et al., 2019). KIRREL1 (NEPH1) localizes to the glomerular slit diaphragm (Liu et al., 2003).

checks.claim: Nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is an autosomal recessive kidney disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified and characterized two novel recessive mutations in KIRREL1 gene in two patients with SRNS of 2 unrelated consanguineous families
checks.explanation: Recessive mutations, homozygous in consanguineous families.

checks.claim: NPHS23 presents with proteinuria.
checks.evidence_quote: He has never achieved a complete remission and remained having undulating proteinuria with partial response to treatment.

checks.claim: NPHS23 presents with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients with detected homozygous mutations in KIRREL1 shared the phenotype of SRNS.

checks.claim: Renal biopsy in NPHS23 may show focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) or other glomerular changes.
checks.evidence_quote: Renal histology of individual B742_21 with KIRREL1 mutation shows focal segmental glomerular sclerosis (arrows) on light microscopy (MPAS staining).
checks.explanation: The other patient showed mesangial hypercellularity consistent with minimal change disease.

checks.claim: KIRREL1 (NEPH1) localizes to the glomerular slit diaphragm.
checks.evidence_quote: we localize the expression of Neph1 to the glomerular slit diaphragm by immunogold electron microscopy in rodents
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that Neph1 localizes to the glomerular slit diaphragm. It shows this in rodents.

paragraphs.text: Solanki et al. (2019) reported 2 patients from 2 unrelated consanguineous families who had steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) beginning in childhood. Renal biopsies showed glomerular lesions, including FSGS.

checks.claim: Solanki et al. (2019) reported 2 patients with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) from 2 unrelated families.
checks.evidence_quote: We discovered two homozygous missense mutations (p.Arg440Cys and p.Ser573Leu) of the KIRREL1 gene in two individuals of unrelated consanguineous families (A666 and B742) with SRNS.

checks.claim: The 2 families with KIRREL1-related SRNS reported by Solanki et al. (2019) were consanguineous.
checks.evidence_quote: two individuals of unrelated consanguineous families (A666 and B742) with SRNS

checks.claim: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in the 2 patients reported by Solanki et al. (2019) began in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient A666_21 was diagnosed with NS at age of 5 years. He developed SRNS at his initial presentation
checks.explanation: The second patient was diagnosed at 14 years; the paper calls both 'affected children'.

checks.claim: Renal biopsies in the 2 patients with SRNS reported by Solanki et al. (2019) showed glomerular lesions, including FSGS.
checks.evidence_quote: Renal histology of individual B742_21 with KIRREL1 mutation shows focal segmental glomerular sclerosis (arrows) on light microscopy (MPAS staining).
checks.explanation: Both biopsies showed glomerular findings (mesangial hypercellularity in both, FSGS in one).

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of NPHS23 in the families reported by Solanki et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of NPHS23 in the families reported by Solanki et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified and characterized two novel recessive mutations in KIRREL1 gene in two patients with SRNS of 2 unrelated consanguineous families

paragraphs.text: In 2 patients with SRNS from unrelated consanguineous families, Solanki et al. (2019) identified homozygous missense mutations in the KIRREL1 gene. In functional studies, both mutant KIRREL1 proteins were mislocalized compared with wildtype and failed to localize to the podocyte cell membrane, indicating defective trafficking.

checks.claim: Solanki et al. (2019) identified homozygous missense mutations in the KIRREL1 gene in 2 patients with SRNS from unrelated consanguineous families.
checks.evidence_quote: We discovered two homozygous missense mutations (p.Arg440Cys and p.Ser573Leu) of the KIRREL1 gene in two individuals of unrelated consanguineous families (A666 and B742) with SRNS.

checks.claim: In functional studies by Solanki et al. (2019), both mutant KIRREL1 proteins were mislocalized compared with wildtype KIRREL1.
checks.evidence_quote: In comparison to the KIRREL1 wild type, a mislocalization of both KIRREL1 mutants (Arg440Cys and Ser573Leu) was noted (Fig.2C).

checks.claim: In functional studies by Solanki et al. (2019), both mutant KIRREL1 proteins failed to localize to the podocyte cell membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that mutant KIRREL1 proteins failed to localize to the podocyte cell membrane, indicating defective trafficking and impaired podocytes function.
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract; the results describe a significantly reduced membrane fraction.

checks.claim: The mislocalization of the mutant KIRREL1 proteins in Solanki et al. (2019) indicated defective trafficking.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that mutant KIRREL1 proteins failed to localize to the podocyte cell membrane, indicating defective trafficking

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2003) noted that Neph1-deficient mice develop nephrotic syndrome at birth, indicating the importance of this protein in the development of a normal glomerular filtration barrier.

checks.claim: Liu et al. (2003) noted that Neph1-deficient mice develop nephrotic syndrome at birth.
checks.evidence_quote: Neph1-deficient mice develop nephrotic syndrome at birth

checks.claim: The nephrotic syndrome in Neph1-deficient mice indicates the importance of Neph1 in the development of a normal glomerular filtration barrier.
checks.evidence_quote: Neph1-deficient mice develop nephrotic syndrome at birth, indicating the importance of this protein in the development of a normal glomerular filtration barrier.

paragraphs.text: Solanki et al. (2019) noted that deletion of Kirrel in a mouse model results in podocyte foot process effacement, causing loss of glomerular filtration function.

checks.claim: Solanki et al. (2019) noted that deletion of Kirrel in a mouse model results in podocyte foot process effacement.
checks.evidence_quote: Deletion of Kirrel in a mouse model results in podocyte foot processes effacement phenotype causing loss of glomerular filtration function.

checks.claim: Solanki et al. (2019) noted that podocyte foot process effacement in Kirrel-deleted mice causes loss of glomerular filtration function.
checks.evidence_quote: Deletion of Kirrel in a mouse model results in podocyte foot processes effacement phenotype causing loss of glomerular filtration function.
